A1.justification: Both ten-page PDFs contain the same GEM paper, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains appendix pages or embedded supplements, despite mentioning an Appendix; all material present supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GEM forecasting, generation, reconstruction, and ablation results on nuScenes, KITTI Odometry, and KITTI-360 in Section 4 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original GEM experiments and quantitative results in Section 4 and Tables 1–6, together with qualitative rollout and controllable-generation demonstrations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same LiDAR tokenizer, dynamic-static separator, tri-path deformable Mamba, gated fusion, diffusion objectives, and optional planner and BEV controls.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes, KITTI Odometry, and KITTI-360 for the same forecasting, distribution-realism, and reconstruction evaluations. Autonomous rollout and controllable-generation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in every corresponding table, including SPFNet and S2Net in Table 1, ST3DCNN in Table 2, and the generation and architecture comparators in Tables 3–6.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same forecasting horizons and historical inputs, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and realism evaluation using 2,000 generated samples. No experimental protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The architecture, component-removal, and tokenizer ablations in Tables 4–6 are unchanged. Scan-path visualizations, autonomous-rollout analysis, and controlled-generation case studies in Figures 4, 6, and 7 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results match. For example, GEM's nuScenes CD remains 0.38 and 0.67 at 1s and 3s, respectively, while KITTI Odometry CD remains 0.17 and 0.28. Reported inference speeds also match.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Equations (1)–(12), and stability-metric definitions in Section 4.1 are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about prediction quality, dynamic-static disentanglement, autonomous rollout, and controllable generation.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.5 retain the same explanations attributing gains to disentanglement and discussing rollout applicability. Qualifications concerning 3s nuScenes AbsRel performance and the slight planning-related performance drop are unchanged.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same optimizers, learning rates, 80-epoch tokenizer training, 1.2-million-step world-model training, and eight H20 GPUs. Architecture details and the project-page link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 57 references, and GEM's positioning relative to previous world models and LiDAR generation methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 8 May 2026 to v2 dated 2 September 2026. Scientific wording, title, author information, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figure 6 receives a tiny size/placement adjustment, with slight vertical shifts in nearby text on page 8; the first-page arXiv stamp also shifts. Figure and table content, captions, labels, and organization remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The supplied PDFs contain identical scientific content, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information. The updated arXiv stamp and tiny layout adjustments do not materially improve or worsen readability or scientific quality.
